method.replay: Each live strategy is driven bar-by-bar with a strictly backward window; entries are simulated at the confirming candle's close and exits from the following candle. Same-candle stop/target uses the conservative stop-first rule unless exact-tiling M1 bars prove the target came first.
method.evaluation_window: bounded backward window per strategy (see strategies[].evaluation_window_bars)
method.position_sizing: repository RiskPolicy + size_position (no fixed pip value assumed)

transaction_costs.model: net = gross - spread_cost; spread_cost = measured per-trade spread price * volume (one full width per closed trade). Commission and swap are not modelled in the headline.

scenarios.label: Repository defaults (primary)
scenarios.note: The repository's configured risk policy, entry cap and daily profit target, used unchanged. This is the reference scenario; no setting is overridden.

scenarios.label: Conservative comparison (explicitly configured)
scenarios.note: Labeled comparison scenario requested by the brief: 0.25% risk per trade, 1% daily loss limit, one open position, at most four new entries per risk day, a 1.5 minimum planned reward/risk and the same $10 daily profit stop. Strategy-specific stop/target/confirmation rules are unchanged; only account-level numbers are tightened.

chronological_split.method: Trades are assigned to development / validation / out-of-sample by entry time (60% / 20% / 20%). Strategy rules were already frozen in code; the out-of-sample window was not used to tune anything.

limitations: One symbol (XAUUSD) and one six-month regime; results do not generalise.
Simulated trades are hypothetical, not broker fills; they are distinct from live signals, shadow validation and real orders.
Commission and swap are not modelled in the headline net; cost is the measured per-bar spread.
The equity/drawdown and daily limits are simulated on gross entry/exit; the per-bar spread is the only cost applied to the running balance.
A small closed-trade count cannot support a profitability conclusion; insufficient evidence is reported rather than a claim.
The implemented EMA pullback is single-timeframe (it reads only the timeframe it is evaluated on); the rules doc describes a multi-timeframe variant. The implemented rule is what is tested here.
order_submission: Not called. No MetaTrader order-execution function is imported.
